app.title: AI Materials Screening
app.summary: A person uploads a CSV of candidate chemical compositions. They check its row, column and duplicate counts against a preview, then run a batch screening. Each row gets a calibrated stability probability, a predictive uncertainty, an out-of-distribution risk, a review flag and a combined candidate score. They narrow the ranked table by prediction, review status and threshold sliders, read summary charts, and export the filtered shortlist as CSV or JSON. They can also check one formula on its own with its top feature contributions, or reopen past batch runs from a saved history.

task.text: Score a list of candidate compositions with a calibrated stability model and pick out a ranked shortlist, with flagged rows set aside for expert review before costly follow-up.

data.text: A table of candidate chemical formulas with any extra user columns. Each row gets model outputs (probability, uncertainty, out-of-distribution risk, score, validation message), and each run is saved to a history.
data.item: a candidate chemical composition (one row of the uploaded CSV)

stage.text: prioritising candidate compositions for review before DFT or experimental follow-up

mechanism.text: Tabs switch between an overview, a single-formula check, batch screening, the run history and a model card. On the batch tab, an uploaded CSV is checked and previewed, scored through a local API, and then shown as a ranked table with dropdown and slider filters and a download button for the filtered rows, with a scatter plot, a top-ten bar chart and histograms of the scores below it.

field.text: machine-learning stability screening of inorganic compositions in materials science

workflow.name: score a list of candidates with a model and export a ranked, filtered shortlist

steps.here: Upload a CSV that must have a composition column. A sample CSV can be downloaded, and the file is checked for readability, the required column and at least one row.
Row, column and duplicate-formula counts are shown with a 20-row preview before the Run batch screening button.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each formula is validated and featurised, then scored with a calibrated stability probability, entropy uncertainty, out-of-distribution risk with a review flag, and a weighted candidate score. Invalid rows are kept with a validation message.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Dropdowns for Prediction (Stable, Unstable, Invalid) and Review, plus sliders for minimum probability, maximum uncertainty and maximum out-of-distribution risk, narrow a table ordered by rank.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Count tiles for candidates, valid, invalid and review-recommended rows; a probability-vs-uncertainty scatter coloured by out-of-distribution risk with hover names; a top-10 score bar chart; and histograms of each score.
Download the filtered ranked table as screening_results.csv or screening_results.json.
Every batch run is saved to a local database. The history tab lists runs with their counts and model version, and a selected run's results can be reopened.

distinctive: Three signals stay separate next to the combined score: a calibrated probability, a predictive uncertainty, and an out-of-distribution risk that flags rows for manual review when they fall outside the training data.
The candidate score is a stated weighted sum (stability, certainty, in-distribution proximity), and the interface notes that it is not a physical property.
Invalid formulas and duplicate rows are kept and marked instead of stopping the batch, so the exported table still accounts for every input row.
A single formula can be checked on its own with its top model feature contributions, labelled as supporting stability or instability, plus a caution that these are not physical causes.
A model card tab reports held-out test metrics, including calibration error, and the tool's intended use and limits.
